<h1><span id="ctl00_mainContent_Label1">Announcements</span></h1>
<div id="announcementsX">
<div id="ctl00_mainContent_ContentBlock1">
<ul> <li> <strong>Submit your abstract and register for the <a href="/meeting2020/">2020 ASBMB Annual Meeting</a> taking place April 4–7 in San Diego.</strong> <br/> <br/> </li> <li> <strong>ASBMB members may submit <a href="/SpecialSymposia/Proposals/">proposals for symposia</a> to be held in 2021. The deadline is Nov. 1.</strong> <br/> <br/> </li> </ul>

<h1><a href="/NewsByCategory.aspx" style="text-decoration:none"> ASBMB News</a> </h1>
<span id="ctl00_mainContent_ListSummary1"><div class="newsHome"><a class="title" href="/News.aspx?id=81732">ASBMB Today October 2019</a><teaser><p>This month, we look at how the founder of Impossible Foods used biochemistry to build a beefy-tasting plant-based burger.  Also, meet Elaine Fuchs, one of the first researchers to study skin-derived stem cells, and Sandhya Visweswariah, a biochemist and groundbreaker for women in India.</p><p><a href="http://www.asbmb.org/asbmbtoday/201910/" target="_blank" title="Read the October 2019 issue of ASBMB Today">Read the October issue</a>.</p></teaser></div><div class="newsHome"><a class="title" href="/News.aspx?id=81500">Science policy podcast</a><teaser><p> Listen to the newest episode of Pipettes &amp; Politics  to learn about the impact of continuing resolutions on federally funded academic research and the potential stalling effects of recent developments in politics on the fiscal year 2020 appropriations process.</p></teaser></div></span>
<!--64/live-70 -->
<br/>
<h1><a href="/NewsByCategory.aspx?catId=186&amp;path=%5cNews%5cJournal+News&amp;__taxonomyshowall=1" style="text-decoration:none">Journal News</a></h1>
<span id="ctl00_mainContent_ListSummary11"><div class="newsHome"><a class="title" href="/News.aspx?id=81049">New JLR virtual issue on lipoprotein (a)</a><teaser>JLR Junior Associate Editor Gissette Reyes-Soffer highlights the work of early career researchers seeking to further our understanding of lipoprotein (a) pathophysiology.</teaser></div><div class="newsHome"><a class="title" href="/News.aspx?id=81031">Special issue of MCP: Multiomics studies of cancer</a><teaser>Researchers surfing this multiomics wave report a plethora of new tools and approaches this month in a special issue of the journal Molecular &amp; Cellular Proteomics devoted to integrating multiple omics.</teaser></div></span>
<br/>
<h1><a href="/NewsByCategory.aspx?catId=140&amp;path=%5cNews%5cMember+News&amp;__taxonomyshowall=1" style="text-decoration:none">Member News</a></h1>
<span id="ctl00_mainContent_ListSummary21"><div class="newsHome"><a class="title" href="/News.aspx?id=81501">New books</a><teaser><p>Read up on some of the  latest books written by ASBMB members , including Bill Sullivan's "Pleased to Meet Me: Genes, Germs, and the Curious Forces That Make Us Who We Are."</p></teaser></div><div class="newsHome"><a class="title" href="/News.aspx?id=81032">In memoriam: Boyd O’Dell (1916–2019)</a><teaser>Boyd O’Dell, one of the first scientists to reveal the important roles that folic acid and vitamin B12 play in development, died April 21. He was 102.</teaser></div></span>
